content:
Three facts power practically every Triangles question: angle sum 180°, the exterior angle theorem, and the triangle inequality. The chapter is small. The mileage is enormous. Scroll down for the free IMO Class 7 Triangles online test. Ten Olympiad-pattern MCQs, instant scoring. Under every question sits an explanation you can learn from.

What the IMO asks from Triangles in Class 7

  • Angle sum property and exterior angle theorem.
  • Classifying triangles by sides and angles.
  • Medians and altitudes.
  • Triangle inequality: can 3, 4, 8 form a triangle?
  • Pythagoras property in right triangles (3-4-5 families).

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Exterior angle = sum of the two INTERIOR OPPOSITE angles.
  • Sides 3, 4, 5 make a right triangle: 3² + 4² = 5².
  • Any side must be shorter than the sum of the other two.
  • In an isosceles triangle with AB = BC and ∠B = 40°, each base angle is 70°.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Adding the wrong pair for the exterior angle theorem.
  • Calling a 3, 4, 8 "triangle" (3 + 4 < 8 — impossible).
  • Assuming the longest side is opposite the smallest angle.

quiz.title: IMO Class 7 Triangles Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. It is:
questions.explanation: All sides differ, so it is scalene. 3² + 4² = 25 = 5², so by Pythagoras it is right-angled.

questions.q: A triangle with angles 30°, 60° and 90° is right-angled. The side opposite the 90° angle is called the:
questions.explanation: The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse — always the longest side.

questions.q: In an isosceles triangle each base angle is twice the vertical angle. The vertical angle is:
In ΔPQR the exterior angles at P and Q are 150° and 130°. Then ∠R is:
questions.explanation: Interior angles: P = 30°, Q = 50°. ∠R = 180 − 80 = 100° — obtuse-angled triangle.

questions.q: In ΔPQR, ∠P = 80°, ∠Q = 55° and PS ⊥ QR. Then ∠RPS is:
In ΔABC, ∠A = 50° and ∠B = 60°. The internal bisectors of ∠A and ∠B meet at I. Then ∠AIB is:
A triangle has sides 7 cm, 24 cm, 25 cm. Its area is:
questions.explanation: 7² + 24² = 625 = 25² — right-angled with legs 7 and 24. Area = ½ × 7 × 24 = 84 cm².

questions.q: The centroid of ΔPQR is G(4, 5) and P is (1, 2). The midpoint S of QR is:
questions.explanation: G divides PS with PG : GS = 2 : 1, so G = (P + 2S)/3. (12, 15) = (1, 2) + 2S gives S = (5.5, 6.5).

questions.q: In ΔABC, ∠A = 80° and ∠B = 40°. The internal bisector of ∠A and the external bisector of ∠B meet at O. Then ∠AOB is:
questions.explanation: O is the excentre opposite A: ∠OAB = 40° and ∠OBA = 20° + 90° = 110°. ∠AOB = 180 − 150 = 30° = ∠C/2.
